title: Torus automorphism actions on connected groups are detected on tangent spaces
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $H$ be a connected affine $k$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $T\simeq\mathbf G_{m,k}^r$, $r\geq0$, be a split torus, where $\mathbf G_m(B)=B^\times$. Suppose $a:T\times_kH\to H$ is an action by group-scheme automorphisms, meaning that $a(1,h)=h$, $a(tu,h)=a(t,a(u,h))$, and $a(t,hh')=a(t,h)a(t,h')$ on all algebra-valued points. Write $\mathfrak h=T_{H/k,e}$ for the tangent space at the identity [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space], with its induced $T$-representation: for every commutative $k$-algebra $B$ and $t\in T(B)$ it is the differential at the identity of $a(t,-):H_B\to H_B$. Then $a$ is the projection $T\times_kH\to H$ if and only if this entire $T$-representation on $\mathfrak h$ is trivial. Triviality of the representation means identity linear maps after every commutative algebra extension, not vanishing of its differential. The group $H$ may be nonreduced and need not be smooth or reductive.

source.place: Proposition 3.3.8 proof, printed p.102, paragraph beginning Since T is of multiplicative type: the connected finite-type group version, explicitly used for the possibly nonreduced identity component of the adjoint kernel. Conrad cites CGP Corollary A.8.11 here. Read online; local Conrad and CGP copies WANTED.

proof.text: Assume the tangent representation is trivial. Apply [lem-sfb-universal-fixed-subscheme] to the $T$-action on $H$ to obtain the closed fixed subscheme $F\hookrightarrow H$. The schemes are separated: on an affine scheme its diagonal is the closed immersion given by the surjective multiplication map on coordinate rings. For every $k$-algebra $B$, $F(B)$ is a subgroup of $H(B)$, since the action fixes the identity and preserves multiplication and inverses after every algebra extension. Thus $F$ is a closed subgroup by [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], and $e\in F(k)$. Put $R=\mathcal O_{H,e}$, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$. By [lem-sfb-rational-point-thickenings-base-change], $R$ is Noetherian local with residue $k$. By [lem-sfb-torus-fixed-local-ideal-jets], the local map to $F$ is $R\to R/J$, where $J=(t^*f-f:t\in T(k),f\in\mathfrak m)$; each $R/\mathfrak m^{n+1}$ and its ideal $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^{n+1}$ carry the stated finite-dimensional rational representations, with equivariant quotient to $V=\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$.

source.place: Theorem 7.1, printed pp.138-139; Lemma 13.4 and proof of Lemma 13.6, printed pp.255-256; fixed-point jet construction of Proposition 8.9, p.150. No smoothness is used in these cited local constructions.

proof.text: For $t\in T(k)$ apply [lem-sc-rational-tangent-cotangent-duality] to the $k$-automorphism $a(t,-):H\to H$ fixing $e$. Its tangent map is identity by hypothesis, so the dual of its induced map on $V$ is identity. Since $V$ is finite-dimensional by step 1, its coordinate functionals separate vectors; hence $t^*|_V=\mathrm{id}$. This uses the entire tangent representation, and makes no inference from a vanishing Lie-algebra differential.

source.place: Tags 0B2E (lemma-tangent-space-rational-point) and 0B2F (lemma-map-tangent-spaces), applied at the rational identity.

proof.text: Fix $n\geq1$. Apply [lem-sfb-gm-representation-weight-basis] successively to the $r$ commuting multiplicative-group factors on each of $V$ and $W_n=\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^{n+1}$ from step 1. Each factor preserves the weight spaces of the preceding factors, since its coaction commutes with theirs; comparison of Laurent monomial coefficients proves this assertion. This gives simultaneous integer weights, and equivariant maps preserve them by the same coefficient comparison. All weights of $V$ are zero: step 2 fixes every rational point; for a nonzero integer exponent $a$, some $z\in k^\times$ satisfies $z^a\ne1$, since $k$ is infinite and a nonzero polynomial has finitely many roots. Choose a basis $v_1,\ldots,v_d$ of $V$. In any preimage of $v_i$ under $W_n\twoheadrightarrow V$, its weight-zero component still maps to $v_i$. Call this component $w_i$, and lift it to $u_i\in\mathfrak m$. The $w_i$ generate $R/\mathfrak m^{n+1}$ as a $k$-algebra: first express an element of $\mathfrak m$ linearly in the $u_i$ modulo $\mathfrak m^2$; in its remainder, replace each factor by that linear expression, increasing the residual degree; after degree $n$ the remainder vanishes. Every generator $w_i$ and scalar is fixed by the full torus coaction, so this jet algebra has trivial torus action. For $d=0$ the same degree-raising argument says that the jet algebra is $k$; for $r=0$ its action is already the identity.

source.place: Theorem 12.12 and Remark 12.13, printed pp.234-235; weight-zero specialization of the lifting argument in the proof of Lemma 13.6, printed p.256. The truncated algebra generation argument does not require regularity.

proof.text: Step 3 implies $t^*f-f\in\mathfrak m^{n+1}$ for every $t\in T(k)$, $f\in\mathfrak m$, and $n\geq1$. Thus $J\subseteq\bigcap_{n\geq1}\mathfrak m^{n+1}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-krull-intersection-jacobson] with the Noetherian local ring $R$, ideal $\mathfrak m$, and cyclic module $R$. Its maximal ideal is its Jacobson radical. The intersection is zero; deleting exponents $0,1$ does not change it because the powers are nested. Consequently $J=0$, and the actual local-ring map $\mathcal O_{H,e}\to\mathcal O_{F,e}$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 00IQ, lemma-intersection-powers-ideal-module, part (2); the jet/Krull method also occurs in Milne Proposition 8.9, printed p.150.

proof.text: The closed subgroup $F\hookrightarrow H$ satisfies [lem-sfb-closed-subgroup-identity-stalk-detection]: $H$ is affine, finite type and connected over the algebraically closed field $k$, and step 4 proves the identity-stalk condition. Hence $F=H$ as group schemes. The restricted-action clause of [lem-sfb-universal-fixed-subscheme] now says that $a:T\times_kH\to H$ is the projection. In particular this is an equality of morphisms and remains true on all algebra-valued points, including nonreduced algebras.

source.place: Translation/homogeneity argument of 1.8, printed p.9, and Theorem 7.1, pp.138-139; general identity-stalk criterion isolated as a separate supporting node.

proof.text: Conversely, if $a$ is the projection, then after any commutative $k$-algebra extension $B$ and for every $t\in T(B)$, the automorphism $a(t,-):H_B\to H_B$ is identity. Its tangent map is identity: by [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space] it sends a dual-number point $\theta$ to $\mathrm{id}\circ\theta=\theta$. This is precisely triviality of the entire representation in the statement.
